subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Compound Interest — Growth, Depreciation and Half-yearly (W10 B2)

questions.stem: Find the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A = 10000×(1.1)² = 10000×1.21 = ₹12,100. CI = 12100−10000 = ₹2,100. Compare: SI would be ₹2,000. The extra ₹100 = interest on first year's interest (10%×₹1,000). Trap: ₹2,000 is the simple interest, not compound interest.

questions.stem: What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Short Trick: for 2 years, Difference = P×(r/100)² = 5000×(0.08)² = 5000×0.0064 = ₹32. Verify: SI = 5000×8×2/100 = ₹800. CI = 5000×(1.08²−1) = 5000×0.1664 = ₹832. Difference = 32 ✓. Trap: ₹40 = P×r²/100 (uses r not r/100).

questions.stem: A sum amounts to ₹4,840 in 2 years and ₹5,324 in 3 years at compound interest. Find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Amount at year 3 / Amount at year 2 = (1+r/100). 5324/4840 = 1.1. r = 10%. Key insight: in consecutive years, the ratio of amounts equals (1+r/100). Trap: students who try to find P first spend unnecessary steps; the ratio directly gives the rate.

questions.stem: At what rate of compound interest (per annum) will ₹2,000 amount to ₹2,420 in 2 years?
questions.explanation: C is correct. 2000×(1+r/100)² = 2420. (1+r/100)² = 1.21. (1+r/100) = 1.1. r = 10%. Note that 1.21 = 1.1² is a key perfect square to recognise. Trap: 8% gives 2000×1.08² = 2332.8 (not 2420); 11% gives 2000×1.11² = 2464.2 (over).

questions.stem: The population of a town is 50,000. It grows at 4% per annum. What will the population be after 2 years?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Population = 50000×(1.04)² = 50000×1.0816 = 54,080. Trap: 54,000 = 50000×1.08 (applies 8% simple interest for 2 years, not compound); 55,000 = 50000×1.10 (uses 10% wrongly).

questions.stem: Find the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 15% per annum for 2 years 4 months, compounded annually.
questions.explanation: B is correct. For 2 full years: A = 8000×(1.15)² = 8000×1.3225 = ₹10,580. For the remaining 4 months (= 1/3 year), use simple interest on ₹10,580: SI = 10580×15×(1/3)/100 = 10580/20 = ₹529. Total CI = (10580+529)−8000 = 11109−8000 = ₹3,109. Rule: for fractional year after full years, apply SI on the last amount. Trap: ₹2,980 uses SI for 2 years only.

questions.stem: The CI on a sum for 2 years at 4% per annum is ₹102. Find the simple interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Difference (CI−SI) for 2 years = P×(r/100)² = P×0.0016 = CI−SI. CI = P×(1.04²−1) = 0.0816P = 102 → P = ₹1,250. SI = 1250×4×2/100 = ₹100. Short Trick: SI/CI ratio for 2 years = 200/(200+r) = 200/204. CI = 102 → SI = 102×200/204 = ₹100. Trap: ₹98 uses SI/CI = 49/51 (wrong ratio).

questions.stem: A machine depreciates at 10% per annum. Its present value is ₹1,62,000. What was its value 2 years ago?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Current = Original × (1−0.10)² → 162000 = V×0.81 → V = 162000/0.81 = ₹2,00,000. Rule: for depreciation, work backwards by dividing by (1−r/100)^t. Trap: ₹1,80,000 = 162000×(1+10×2/100) (applies SI in reverse); ₹1,96,000 = 162000/0.9 (only goes back 1 year).

questions.stem: What principal will amount to ₹9,261 in 3 years at 5% compound interest per annum?
A sum of money at compound interest doubles itself in 4 years. In how many years will it become 8 times?
questions.explanation: C is correct. If P doubles in 4 years, then 2P in 4 years → 4P in 8 years → 8P in 12 years. Rule: 8 = 2³, so it takes 3 doubling periods = 3×4 = 12 years. Short Trick: if sum becomes n times in t years at CI, it becomes nᵏ times in k×t years. Here n=2, nᵏ=8=2³, so k=3, time=3×4=12. Trap: 16 years = 4×4 (wrongly calculates 2×2×2×2 steps).
